title: Projects, Assets, Quality and CRM
subtitle: The modules that stop being optional once you pass twenty people
outcomes: Bill project work from timesheets without an Excel reconciliation
Run a fixed-asset register with depreciation and disposal
Put quality gates where they catch defects, not where they look good
Turn leads into quotations with a pipeline you can forecast

slides.title: Projects are a cost collector with a Gantt chart
bullets: Project groups tasks; every timesheet, purchase and expense that references it joins the same profitability view
Tasks carry dependencies, expected hours and actual time; the Gantt view is for coordination, not for planning theory
Project templates create the standard phases for repeatable delivery work
Project type controls billing: fixed price, time and materials, or non-billable internal work
slides.notes: Projects pay for themselves the first time someone asks whether a client is profitable. The prerequisite is discipline: every cost and every hour must reference the project. If a timesheet does not name the project, that hour is invisible forever. Make the project field mandatory on timesheets for billable teams.

slides.title: From timesheet to invoice
bullets: Timesheets record hours per employee per activity; billing rates come from the activity's costing rate and the project or customer
Project billing lets you invoice billable hours from a Sales Invoice using 'Get items from timesheet'
Fixed-price projects bill against milestones instead, with the project as the revenue dimension
Project profitability compares billed value against labour, expenses and purchases booked to the project
slides.notes: The billing decision is a contract question: are you selling hours or outcomes? Time and materials needs rate discipline and weekly timesheet approval; fixed price needs milestone discipline and a hard review of scope creep. Set the project type honestly at creation, because retrofitting a billing model into an invoiced project is painful and always late.

callout.title: Approve weekly
callout.text: Unapproved timesheets block billing. Weekly approval cadence turns a month-end scramble into a ten-minute review.

slides.title: A register, not a spreadsheet
bullets: Asset Category defines depreciation method, useful life and the accounts used for depreciation and disposal
Purchase a fixed asset through a Purchase Invoice with 'Is Fixed Asset', or create the asset and capitalise it from a work order
Depreciation runs from the schedule automatically or via manual entries; the accumulated depreciation account grows while asset cost stays
Disposal, sale, movement between locations and repairs are separate documents — that is what makes the register auditable
slides.notes: The classic asset failure is a purchase invoice expensed because nobody flagged the item as a fixed asset. Then depreciation is computed in a spreadsheet and the balance sheet drifts. Put a review step on purchases of capital items, and reconcile the asset register to the fixed-asset cost accounts quarterly.

rows: Gain or loss computed and posted

slides.title: Quality gates where they catch things
bullets: Quality Inspection Template lists parameters with numeric or pass/fail goals per item
Trigger inspections on purchase receipt, delivery note or job card — the earliest point that can still stop the problem
Inspection results feed QC actions: accept, reject, rework or return to supplier
A quality system that measures everything and blocks nothing is documentation, not control
slides.notes: Choose two or three parameters that predict customer complaints and make them hard gates. More parameters mean more skipped fields. For Malaysian manufacturers supplying into regulated chains, the inspection record is also the evidence trail customers audit; keep the readings, not just the pass mark.
paths: Stock > Item > Inspection Required Before Purchase

slides.title: Leads, opportunities and an honest pipeline
bullets: Lead captures an unqualified contact; Opportunity tracks a qualified deal with value, probability and expected closing date
Convert an opportunity to a Quotation to keep the attribution chain from first contact to revenue
Territory, campaign and source dimensions answer where the revenue came from
Pipeline reporting is only useful if stages and probabilities are enforced and reviewed weekly
slides.notes: Most small businesses already have a CRM: a salesperson's phone. ERPNext wins when the pipeline feeds quotations and orders, so the forecast matches the order book. Enforce two rules: every quotation has an opportunity, and every salesperson updates stage and date weekly. Without that, the CRM becomes a graveyard of stale records.

callout.title: Forecast from the order book
callout.text: Compare expected opportunity value to submitted sales orders monthly. The gap is your pipeline realism score.

slides.title: Issues, SLAs and warranty claims
bullets: Issues record customer complaints with priority, status and resolution time; service level agreements set response targets
Escalation rules raise priority automatically when an SLA is about to breach
Warranty claims link the issue to the serial number and, when covered, to a free-of-charge delivery and repair
Track resolution time by technician and product — that is where service margin hides
slides.notes: Support data is the cheapest product feedback you will ever get. If the same serial number fails repeatedly, you have a manufacturing or supplier problem, not a service problem. Review the top five failure modes monthly and route them back to quality and purchasing.

slides.title: The joins that make the modules worth having
bullets: Project + timesheet + invoice = project profitability without a spreadsheet
Asset + purchase invoice + depreciation = a fixed-asset register that ties to the GL
Item + quality inspection + warranty claim = traceable failure history per product
Opportunity + quotation + sales order = revenue attribution from first touch to cash
slides.notes: Each module is modest alone; the value is in the joins. When someone asks why they should use projects or assets at all, show them the join, not the form. A single report that answers a question the business actually asks is a better argument than any feature list.

callout.title: Capital allowances
callout.text: The asset register is also your capital allowance working paper. Keep acquisition dates, categories and disposal records clean.

slides.title: Adoption rules that keep these modules alive
bullets: Make the project field mandatory on timesheets and expenses for billable teams
Flag capital purchases at the item level so the asset register is not rebuilt at year end
Inspect at receipt for incoming goods and at job card for produced goods
Require an opportunity on every quotation and a weekly stage update
slides.notes: Every module in this chapter dies quietly when the mandatory field is optional. ERPNext can enforce most of these with property setters, mandatory flags or workflow conditions. Choose enforcement over exhortation; a field that blocks submission gets filled, a field that politely suggests does not.

lab.title: Bill a project, register an asset, gate quality, win a deal
steps: Create a Project with three tasks and a fixed-price billing type; log two timesheets against it with billable hours
Raise a Sales Invoice from the project using timesheet billing and confirm the project profitability report shows labour cost against billed value
Create an Asset Category with straight-line depreciation over five years, then capitalise one purchase as a fixed asset
Run depreciation for one month and verify the accumulated depreciation account moved while the asset cost did not
Create a Quality Inspection Template for a purchased component and trigger it on a Purchase Receipt; record a failing reading and reject the receipt
Create a Lead, convert it to an Opportunity worth MYR 50,000 at 40% probability, then convert it to a Quotation
Review the pipeline report and reconcile the opportunity value against the quotation you just created
lab.done: Four joins work end to end: project to invoice, purchase to asset, inspection to rejection, and lead to quotation.

quiz.question: What must be true for project profitability to be trustworthy?
options: Every cost and hour references the project
Only invoices use the project field
quiz.why: Unreferenced costs are invisible to the profit report, so the project field must be mandatory on time and expenses.

quiz.question: A machine bought last month was expensed. What is the consequence?
options: Assets and equity are understated, expenses overstated, and depreciation is missing
Only the cash flow statement is wrong
quiz.why: Capital expenditure was treated as a period expense, so the register and depreciation schedule will not match the GL.

quiz.question: Where is the most useful place to trigger a quality inspection?
options: At the earliest point where a defect can still be stopped — receipt for incoming, job card for produced
quiz.why: Inspections are controls; the value is preventing bad material from reaching the customer or the next production step.

quiz.question: Which practice keeps a CRM pipeline usable?
options: An opportunity behind every quotation plus a weekly stage review
quiz.why: Attribution only exists if quotations link to opportunities, and forecasts decay without a regular review cadence.

quiz.question: How should a project's billing model be decided?
options: At project creation, because it determines timesheet, milestone and revenue handling
quiz.why: Fixed price versus time and materials changes what you record and how you invoice; retrofitting it mid-project is expensive.

narration: Chapter eight covers the modules that stop being optional once a company passes twenty people. Projects are a cost collector with a Gantt chart attached. Every hour, purchase and expense that references the project joins the same profitability view, which means the project field must be mandatory on timesheets and expenses; an hour that does not name its project is invisible forever. Decide the billing model at creation, time and materials or fixed price, because it changes what you record and how you invoice. Assets exist so you never rebuild depreciation in a spreadsheet: capitalise through a purchase invoice flagged as a fixed asset, let the category drive the schedule, and treat movement, disposal and repair as separate documents. Reconcile the register to the fixed-asset accounts quarterly. For quality, choose two or three parameters that predict customer complaints and make them hard gates at receipt and at the job card; a system that measures everything and blocks nothing is documentation, not control. For CRM, one opportunity behind every quotation plus a weekly stage update keeps the pipeline useful. Support data is the cheapest product feedback you own: repeated serial failures are a supplier or manufacturing problem, not a service problem. The value of these modules is in the joins, so show the report, not the form.
